newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Progen says drug reduces cancer growth.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Progen says drug reduces cancer growth.

text.p: Biotechnology company Progen Industries Ltd said on Thursday it had received encouraging results in the treatment of primary human tumours transplanted to mice with its anti-cancer compound PI-88.
Progen said a single daily injection of PI-88 significantly inhibited the growth rate of human colon cancer in the mice.
No toxic side effects were observed, it said.

Progen, which was floated in 1995, has spent about A$1 million a year to fund research into developing an anti-cancer compound at the John Curtin School of Medical Research at the Australian National University.
Progen research and development manager Robert Don said the company would complete side-effect studies, and hoped to begin human trials by the end of the year.
Don said Progen selected PI-88 as its preferred compound last year and began studies in the fourth quarter to examine its effect on rapidly growing primary human tumours.
Preliminary results indicated that PI-88, which works by attacking the life support system for cancers, significantly inhibited the growth rate of a human colon cancer transplanted to mice.

Earlier studies had shown that PI-88 also inhibited the spread of secondary cancers in experimental animals, indicating it could be effective against both primary cancer and the spread of secondary cancers in humans, Progen said.
"These results are very encouraging and increase our confidence levels for measurable outcomes in human clinical trials," the company said in a statement.
Research was continuing to examine the effects of different dose levels and methods of drug administration.
Progen had previously estimated the sales potential for the product could exceed A$1 billion a year, based on five percent of the world market, if it meets all regulatory testing regimes.
Progen's share price rose sharply in early trade, to be up 17 cents to 91 cents by 11.05 a.m. (0005 GMT).
